findings.rule: A prompt that opens with the review driver's marker, `PANDO-REVIEW: «pass» tier=«tier»` on a line of its own, is now the composer's third receiver.
findings.input:
A prompt whose first line is ordinary user text and whose fifth line is the marker, e.g. "Please check the routine prompt I saved:

```text
PANDO-REVIEW: spec-fidelity tier=opus
```
" — the prompt does not open with the marker, yet find_review returns Review("spec-fidelity", "opus", None), compose sets resolved["role"] = "reviewer" and renders the pass file's prompt block as the session's task.
findings.finding: find_review uses _REVIEW.search with re.MULTILINE, so any line of the prompt that carries the marker makes the session a review session, while the specification makes only a prompt that opens with the marker the third receiver.

findings.rule: `«n»` filled from whatever names the pull request in the prompt: a `/pull/«n»` URL, `owner/repo#n`, a JSON `number` field, or the words "pull request" followed by a number.
findings.input:
A fire payload that names the pull request by a JSON field and cites an unrelated ticket, e.g. "PANDO-REVIEW: spec-fidelity tier=opus

<routine-fire-payload>
{"number": 26, "body": "ADVANCES pandoscope/skills#195"}
</routine-fire-payload>
" — the owner/repo#n pattern is tried before the JSON `number` pattern and matches `pandoscope/skills#195`, so the composer fills `<n>` with 195 and the rendered task tells the reviewer to review pull request 195, fetch `pull/195/head` and push `claude/review-spec-fidelity-opus-pr195`.
findings.finding: The `owner/repo#n` pattern matches any repo-qualified issue or pull request reference anywhere in the prompt, so a citation that does not name the pull request under review silently wins over a later form that does.
